instruction:
Read docs/TASK_P11_processor.md sections 2.1 and 2.2 (Send Batch, the Transport change) and section 4. Two files. src/processor/types.ts (its current text follows): ONE change, in Transport.fetch's init the member `body: string` becomes `body?: string`; nothing else changes. src/processor/batch.ts, NEW: export `const BATCH_POLL_MS = 15000`, `const BATCH_GRACE_MS = 60000` and `async function sendBatch(config: ProcessorConfig, requests: Request[], transport: Transport): Promise<GenerationResult>` (`import { assembleBatch } from "./batchRequest.js"`, `import { readBatch } from "./batchResponse.js"`, types with `import type` from "../compiler/types.js" and "./types.js"). It calls only transport.fetch and transport.sleep: the submit is ONE POST, never retried; every poll sleeps BATCH_POLL_MS BEFORE its GET, and the GET's init is {method: "GET", headers} with no body key. Answers and usage in the order of the requests, one each; every error text exactly as section 2.2 writes it. Never rejects. Write no test file: a probe tests you and a judge writes the example tests.

## Function Send Batch

One generation as one OpenRouter batch - submit once, poll until done or the wait runs out, map the results back to the requests.

Behaviour: sendBatch(config, requests, transport) never rejects; answers and usage come back in the order of requests, one each; exports BATCH_POLL_MS 15000 and BATCH_GRACE_MS 60000. A request whose model is set and differs from the config's is answered "batch runs one model: <customId> pins <model>, the batch is <config model>" and left out; no request left → no call. Submit: Assemble Batch of the rest, ONE transport.fetch(url, {method POST, headers, body}), never retried (a POST that reached the provider may already be a paid batch), then Read Batch: a thrown fetch → every request "batch submit: transport: <message>"; an error read → "batch submit: <its error>"; no batchId → "batch submit: no batch id". Poll: polls = max(1, floor(timeoutMs / BATCH_POLL_MS)), on this route TIMEOUT_MS is the whole wait; each poll sleeps transport.sleep(BATCH_POLL_MS) first, then transport.fetch(url + "/" + batchId, {method GET, headers}) with no body, then Read Batch. A thrown poll, status 408, 429 or 5xx, and a 404 while poll number × BATCH_POLL_MS ≤ BATCH_GRACE_MS (the provider's read-after-write lag) go on to the next poll; any other error read is final: every request "batch <batchId>: <its error>". pending → the next poll. done or failed → each request takes the first reply with its customId; a request without one → "batch <batchId> <status>: <the batch's error, else 'no result'>". Polls run out → every request "batch <batchId> still <the last status read, the submit's at first> after <polls> polls"; the batch is not cancelled. Every error answer has text and finishReason null, usage 0 and 0 tokens, cost, provider and generationId null.

Steps:
- calls: Assemble Batch
- calls: Read Batch
- produces: Answer
- produces: Usage

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given the batch config (timeoutMs 60000); requests a.v1, b.v1, c.v1, d.v1 (model null); calls answer in turn 202 batchSubmitted.json, 200 batchInProgress.json, 200 batchCompleted.json; when sent; then three calls: POST https://openrouter.ai/api/beta/batches, then twice GET https://openrouter.ai/api/beta/batches/batch-1789576284-Ejahe4wq9AgVdp5xGdNm with no body; sleeps [15000, 15000]; answers in request order: a.v1 text "```ts\nexport const a = 1;\n```" finishReason "stop"; b.v1 text null finishReason "length" error null; c.v1 error "batch item error: context length exceeded"; d.v1 error "batch batch-1789576284-Ejahe4wq9AgVdp5xGdNm completed: no result"; usage a.v1 11030 in, 571 out, cost 0.00269316; d.v1 0, 0, cost null (ref: tests/fixtures/processor/batchConfig.json)
2. given the batch config; request a.v1; calls answer 202 batchSubmitted.json, 404 batchNotFound.json, 200 batchCompleted.json; when sent; then three calls; sleeps [15000, 15000]; answer a.v1 finishReason "stop", error null (a 404 at 15000 ms is inside the grace)
3. given the batch config with timeoutMs 120000; request a.v1; calls answer 202 batchSubmitted.json, four times 200 batchInProgress.json, then 404 batchNotFound.json; when sent; then six calls; sleeps five times 15000; answer error "batch batch-1789576284-Ejahe4wq9AgVdp5xGdNm: http 404: Batch job batch-1789576284-Ejahe4wq9AgVdp5xGdNm not found." (poll 5, 75000 ms, is past the grace)
4. given the batch config; requests a.v1, b.v1; calls answer 202 batchSubmitted.json, then 200 batchFailed.json; when sent; then two calls; both answers error "batch batch-1789576284-Ejahe4wq9AgVdp5xGdNm failed: HTTP 400: invalid batch inference job: job-submission-count for account acct-0000, in use: 16, quota: 16"
5. given the batch config; requests a.v1, b.v1; the submit answers 400 with tests/fixtures/processor/noBatchEndpoint.json; when sent; then one call, no sleep; both answers error "batch submit: http 400: HTTP 400: invalid batch inference job: Model 'z-ai/glm-5.3:batch' does not have a :batch endpoint."
6. given the batch config (timeoutMs 60000); request a.v1; calls answer 202 batchSubmitted.json, then 200 batchInProgress.json every time; when sent; then five calls; sleeps [15000, 15000, 15000, 15000]; answer error "batch batch-1789576284-Ejahe4wq9AgVdp5xGdNm still in_progress after 4 polls", usage 0, 0, cost null
7. given the batch config; requests x.v1 (model "other/m") and a.v1 (model null); calls answer 202 batchSubmitted.json, then a thrown Error("socket hang up"), then 200 batchCompleted.json; when sent; then three calls; the POST body's requests hold only a.v1; answers x.v1 error "batch runs one model: x.v1 pins other/m, the batch is z-ai/glm-5.3:batch", a.v1 finishReason "stop" error null
8. given the batch config with model "acme/m:batch"; requests x.v1 (model "z-ai/glm-5.3:batch") and a.v1 (model null); calls answer 202 batchSubmitted.json, then 200 batchCompleted.json; when sent; then two calls; the POST body's model is "acme/m:batch", its requests hold only a.v1; answers x.v1 error "batch runs one model: x.v1 pins z-ai/glm-5.3:batch, the batch is acme/m:batch" (the batch model is config.model on every path, never a literal), a.v1 finishReason "stop" error null

Data Answer: One model answer to one Request, or its failure.
Schema:
{ customId, text: string | null, finishReason: string | null, error: string | null }

Data Usage: Tokens and cost of one Request as the provider reported them (0 tokens and null cost when it reported none).
Schema:
{ customId, inputTokens, outputTokens, cost: number | null, provider: string | null, generationId: string | null }

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Write the files: `src/processor/types.ts`, `src/processor/batch.ts`.

TypeScript with `strict` on, ESM with NodeNext resolution: every relative import carries the `.js` extension and types are imported with `import type`. No `any`: use `unknown` and narrow. Tests are vitest: `toBe` on scalars and short strings, `toStrictEqual` on a whole result; stubs come from `tests/helpers.ts`, never your own.
